items.text: Nostalgia for failed products is fascinating. If you listen to the nostalgics, there seems to be massive demand, yet if you actually bring the product back, almost nobody buys it.

items.text: The soul isn’t in trait Openness, it’s in the general caring factor, which is something like inverse Dark Triad.

quoted.author: lynchian yuppie
quoted.text:
"I have known 90-IQ people who are curious about the world, and want to learn as much as they can. That’s not a lot, but it’s not like they lacked the basic spark of a soul."

I've known some clever people who ran cognitive circles around everyone in their environment but couldn't be bothered about the world. Just a complete lack of interest in ideas, places, art, even objects. They were company men, interested in ideas that served the firm. I can respect this to some degree. But clearly "the spark" and IQ, while correlated, aren't the same.

items.author: du
items.text: The specific feeling you fall asleep to plays such a crucial role in influencing your mood the next morning. Regardless of what happened during the day, be unwavering consistent with those 5-10 minutes every night and it legitimately transforms your life

items.author: J.K. Lundblad | Teaching Progress
items.text:
Progress is doing more with less.

We feared a bare Earth; we got a reforesting one.

We feared smoggy skies and acid rain; we got cleaner air.

We fear climate change; we got declining carbon emissions.

Each step up the energy 🪜 from wood, to coal, to oil, to gas saw in improvement in thermal efficiency, declining pollution, and 30 percent less CO2 per unit of energy.
